Sumitrā
------------------------------------------
Sumitrā was the daughter of Śūra, the king of Magadha. She was the second wife of दशरथ.
See RĀMĀYAṆA for more details.

Sumantu
------------------------------------------
The sage वेदव्यास had four chief disciples to whom he taught the four वेदस्. सुमन्तु was the last of these and received the Atharvaveda from him.
See also JAIMINI, PAILA and VYĀSA.

Sumantra
(‘one [who gives] good advice’)
------------------------------------------
Sumantra was a minister in the cabinet of the king दशरथ. He was also an expert charioteer. He was highly respected for his age and wisdom.
It was he who drove the royal chariot on several important occasions like bringing the sage ऋष्यशृङ्ग for the sacrifice पुत्रकामेष्टि, sending राम to the forest and so on. He too had gone to the forest with भरत, who tried to bring back राम.
Some more persons by the same name are met with in the Mahābhārata: a king of the country of Sauvīra, a sage (descendent of भृगु), the charioteer of अभिमन्यु and a son of Drupada.
